label: Design 2 - Back-Side Living Rebuild + Sunroom Bedroom Replacement
summary: The strongest whole-house move: daily living and dining shift to the brighter back/deck side, the current dining edge becomes a softer chill/reading zone beside the retained kitchen, the current lounge becomes a proper bedroom, laundry and WC move toward separated office-side service rooms, and the current sunroom is replaced by a proper insulated bedroom.
room_changes: Bedroom 2, laundry, toilet, and entrance become a larger living/dining/day room.
The current dining edge becomes a softer chill/reading zone beside the retained kitchen.
The current lounge becomes a proper bedroom rather than a media room.
Laundry and WC move toward the office/bathroom side.
Bathroom, WC, and laundry functions are replanned as separate adjacent rooms rather than one combined laundry/bathroom.
The sunroom is demolished and replaced with a properly insulated bedroom that can push west to align with the master-bedroom wall.
The renovated kitchen stays broadly intact.
daylight_strategy: Put the most-used daytime lounge function where morning-to-early-afternoon light is more valuable.
Stop spending the best back-side daylight on laundry and transient entrance use.
Design the replacement bedroom with controlled glazing, privacy, curtains, and thermal performance rather than repeating the sunroom problem.
Add deck shade and wind control that preserves useful daylight into kitchen/dining.
movement_strategy: Make back/garage arrival feel deliberate rather than secondary.
Improve the route from entry to kitchen, deck, and new lounge.
Reduce the current lounge's role as a circulation junction by making it a private bedroom with a clear doorway.
Keep guest toilet access logical after the WC relocation.
build_scope: Demolish or substantially remove the existing sunroom.
Construct a new insulated bedroom envelope on or near the sunroom site.
Alter internal walls around Bedroom 2, entrance, laundry, and toilet.
Relocate laundry and WC plumbing toward the office/bathroom side while keeping laundry separate from bathing functions.
Upgrade electrical, heating, flooring, and finishes in the changed zones.
Add a designed deck shade or roof solution.
risks: Service-room relocation and office loss make this disruptive and expensive.
The replacement bedroom must not inherit the sunroom's exposure, glare, privacy, heat, and cold problems.
The new living/dining/day room must not become a long narrow leftover room.
The current lounge needs proper bedroom privacy, door position, window placement, and heating before it can work as a sleeping room.
Services, structure, drainage, consent, and staged construction need builder/designer review.
cost_notes: Likely a real architectural renovation rather than a small alteration.
Broad planning band: NZD 140k to 500k+ depending on structure, wet-area relocation, and new bedroom envelope.

furniture_reuse.item: Renovated kitchen cabinetry and main kitchen appliances
furniture_reuse.action: Protect during works and keep the renovated kitchen broadly intact unless later design testing proves a very high-value reason to alter it.
furniture_reuse.cost_note: Avoids turning this into a kitchen-renovation project.

furniture_reuse.action: Relocate the existing dining set into the larger bright rear room so dining no longer occupies the retained kitchen chill edge.
Move the main sitting furniture into the brighter back-side room so the best daytime light supports the most-used daytime living space.

furniture_reuse.item: Lounge TV, fireplace relationship, and media pieces
furniture_reuse.proposed_location: New living/dining/day room or chill/reading edge
furniture_reuse.action: Do not assume the TV/fireplace relationship stays in the current lounge, because that room is now being tested as a bedroom.

furniture_reuse.item: Teen bedroom bed, dresser, bedside table, TV, and loose storage
furniture_reuse.proposed_location: Replacement insulated bedroom on the sunroom site
furniture_reuse.action: Reuse the existing teen-bedroom furniture where it fits, then design the replacement bedroom around privacy, warmth, blackout control, and a calmer storage wall.
Allow for careful removal and reuse of cabinets where dimensions suit the new laundry/WC/storage rooms, accepting that some panels or benchtops may need alteration.
furniture_reuse.cost_note: Can reduce joinery cost, but plumbing and refitting still need a builder/joiner allowance.

furniture_reuse.action: Relocate the existing appliances if their age and condition justify keeping them through the renovation.

furniture_reuse.current_location: Lounge, Bedroom 2, office, and hallway-adjacent rooms
furniture_reuse.proposed_location: Chill/reading edge, living/dining/day room, or replacement bedroom
furniture_reuse.action: Reuse only the pieces that help each room's new purpose; avoid carrying tall storage into the new bright room if it blocks light or circulation.

furniture_reuse.item: Office desk and surplus office storage
furniture_reuse.proposed_location: Kitchen chill/reading edge, replacement bedroom study corner, or off-site
furniture_reuse.action: The office is sacrificed to separated service rooms in this option, so test whether the desk is still needed before forcing it into a poorer room.

furniture_reuse.item: Bedroom storage, blackout/privacy window treatment, and heating for the replacement bedroom
furniture_reuse.proposed_location: Replacement insulated bedroom on the sunroom site
furniture_reuse.action: Budget for the items that make the new bedroom genuinely better than the existing sunroom: robe/storage, curtains or blinds, heating, privacy, and controlled glazing.
furniture_reuse.cost_note: Small compared with building works, but important to avoid recreating the sunroom comfort problem.

furniture_reuse.item: Deck shade, wind control, and outdoor living pieces
furniture_reuse.action: Add a proper shade/wind solution so the deck can support the new living arrangement instead of relying on the current umbrella.
furniture_reuse.cost_note: Can range from a modest pergola/shade-sail package to a more expensive roofed structure.
